feature: Directory integrity file and execution gate
note: Both sums support hash/validate. Native SQL execution gates hashed dirs; compat apply/status/set/new/diff/down do too. Import verifies source sums. Replay uses one verified snapshot and refuses drift.
evidence: /tmp/ptah migrations hash/validate --help; verified create→hash→validate (exit 0) then tampered file→validate exit 1; ptah migrations hash --dir-format atlas wrote atlas.sum. Apply-time gate: a tampered hashed directory refuses on both surfaces before executing anything (stokaro/ptah#955, PR #962). Missing sum file measured 2026-08-01 against Atlas CE v1.2.0 (stokaro/ptah#970): on a directory with no atlas.sum, Atlas exits 1 with `Error: checksum file not found` and never creates the target database; ptah-compat migrate apply now matches that output byte for byte (same code path as ptah-compat migrate validate). The refusal keys on the presence of any *.sql file, also measured: CE gates an unhashed dir holding only foo.sql, and reports `No migration files to execute` at exit 0 for an empty or .gitkeep-only dir. The exemption reads the top level only, on both tools. It used to recurse here, on the ground that Ptah's registrar executed nested files, and that entry documented only the UNHASHED nested shape while saying nothing about the hashed one, which was wide open: measured 2026-08-03 against the pinned Atlas CE v1.3.0, on `1_a.sql` + `sub/2_b.sql` both tools wrote a byte-identical atlas.sum listing ONLY `1_a.sql`, both `migrate validate` exited 0 with empty streams, and then `migrate apply` created table `a` on CE and `a`, `b` AND a `pwned` table appended to the nested file AFTER hashing on ptah-compat — SQL executing that no checksum covered or could cover, at exit 0, on a directory both tools called clean. Fixed in stokaro/ptah#976 by narrowing the loader to the set atlas.sum covers (top level, spelled exactly `.sql`) rather than by adding a refusal, the same consumed-⊆-covered remedy stokaro/ptah#982 applied to the imported layouts; the recursive exemption then had nothing left to protect and came out with it. Post-fix the apply matrix matches CE on every nested and case-variant shape: subonly and mixed, hashed and unhashed, duplicate version across depth, and `1_a.SQL` alone (which used to be REFUSED as `unrecognized SQL files` while `1_a.sql` beside `2_c.SQL` was silently accepted — inconsistent rather than strict). One deliberate divergence remains and it is the only one: ptah-compat names each declined file on stderr (`warning: sub/2_b.sql is not covered by atlas.sum and will not run; Atlas migrations are top-level files named *.sql`) where CE is silent, because CE's silence here IS the defect half — on a subdirectory-only directory CE hashes zero files, validates clean and applies nothing at exit 0, so the author's committed migration never runs and nothing says so. Exit codes and stdout stay byte-identical; only stderr differs. The same narrowing applies to native `ptah --dir-format atlas`, which had the identical hole (measured: base wrote an atlas.sum covering `1_a.sql` and executed `a` and `b`); native auto mode keeps recursing and stays self-consistent because its ptah.sum is computed FROM discovery and covers `sub/2_b.sql` too. Native verbs do not yet print the declined-file warning. Native `ptah migrations up` deliberately stays permissive on a never-hashed directory and reports `migration sum verification failed: atlas.sum not found; run 'ptah migrations hash --dir-format atlas' to create it` only under --verify-sum (exit 2). Directories read through ?format= (goose/flyway/liquibase/dbmate/golang-migrate) are gated on the atlas.sum the SOURCE directory carries, verified before the source layout is parsed and before the database is opened (stokaro/ptah#973, on top of #984 and #992). Measured 2026-08-02 against Atlas CE v1.2.0 with scripts/probe-atlas-apply-gate.sh: five formats x {never hashed, hashed clean, edited, file added, file removed} match CE's exit code and refusal text, with the L<n> line naming the SOURCE file (1_init.up.sql for golang-migrate, V1__init.sql for flyway). The covered set is per layout, so editing a golang-migrate down file, a Flyway undo file, or a file a Flyway baseline squashes is invisible to both tools, and an empty covered set is exempt from the missing-sum refusal (CE exits 0 with `No migration files to execute` on golang-migrate down-only and Flyway undo-only). Flyway is the one layout whose sum reaches into subdirectories, so an unhashed flyway dir holding only sub/V2__nested.sql is refused by both while the same shape read as goose is exempt. Still open on those exempt rows: ptah-compat reports `no importable migration files found` and exits 1 where CE exits 0 (stokaro/ptah#980). The gate is verb-neutral since stokaro/ptah#974: `migrate status` and `migrate set` share the same predicate and the same refusal bytes as apply and validate, measured 2026-08-03 against the pinned Atlas CE v1.3.0 with scripts/probe-atlas-integrity-verbs.sh section 12 over {never hashed, hashed clean, edited, added, removed} plus the empty and non-SQL exemptions, comparing exit code and both streams separately. The refusal precedes the database connection on both verbs and the positional-arity check on set, matching CE. Since stokaro/ptah#1086, `migrate new` and `migrate diff` verify the selected layout's covered set before writing. Re-measured 2026-08-11 in scripts/probe-atlas-integrity-verbs.sh section 14: on unhashed, edited, added and removed Atlas directories both tools refuse with matching output and leave the directory byte-unchanged; on clean, empty, non-SQL, nested and case-variant controls both tools accept and write. The same section now checks all five external layouts through `?format=`: both writers exit 0, change the directory, produce the expected artifact shape and leave output the pinned community binary validates. `migrate import` is gated since stokaro/ptah#1095, under a policy of its own: a source that carries an atlas.sum must verify against it, while a source with no atlas.sum is imported rather than refused. Both halves measured 2026-08-03 against the pinned community binary v1.3.0 on hashed goose, golang-migrate, dbmate, liquibase and flyway sources, under both the ?format= and --dir-format spellings: edited, added, removed and a covered entry that is a DIRECTORY all exit 1 with the same stdout block CE prints, while never-hashed and clean exit 0 and write. Before the fix all 24 tampered rows exited 0 here and wrote the converted directory, then hashed it — so `migrate apply` refused the source while `migrate import` laundered it into a destination `migrate validate` calls clean. The refusal now precedes the destination checks (destination already holding SQL, --to equal to --from), matching CE, and no destination directory is created. A covered entry that cannot be read refuses on an UNHASHED source too, which is what CE does and what an early return on the missing sum would have missed. `migrate lint` accepts an unhashed directory for adoption but refuses drift once a sum exists. Native and formatted compat `migrate down` gate hashed directories; the default/full surface supports the explicit recovery override while strict CE rejects it. Native `generate --replay`, `generate --shadow-db`, `checkpoint`, `baseline`, `test`, `lint`, and `repair --resume-from` resolve the same strict boolean at command entry, verify one immutable snapshot, and execute those same bytes. Generation and checkpoint publication compare their bound output directory with the authorized history before refreshing a sum, so drift cannot be laundered. What the gate verifies is also what apply executes, for every layout, since stokaro/ptah#982: the importer selects the files it converts with the same SumFileNames rule the gate hashes. Before that, Flyway alone ran a wider set - measured 2026-08-02, a superseded baseline (B1 under B2) and a lowercase prefix (v2__evil.sql) both executed on a directory `migrate validate` called clean on BOTH tools, so SQL ran that no checksum covered. scripts/probe-atlas-apply-gate.sh section 9a now asserts parity on both shapes plus a repeatable, a nested migration and a baseline outranking its survivor, comparing the number each tool ran against the covered-set size rather than only against each other.

Volatility is encoded across IS_DETERMINISTIC and SQL_DATA_ACCESS because those are the only catalog columns that survive the read: of the fifteen combinations of the two axes, six are accepted under the pinned image's binary-logging defaults and only two of those are NOT DETERMINISTIC, so IMMUTABLE, STABLE and VOLATILE take three distinct cells. Routine names compare case-insensitively, which is the engines' rule for routines and not the rule their identifier semantics carry for tables. A `language` other than `sql` is named as skipped rather than refused, because Ptah has no way to scope a declared object to a dialect (stokaro/ptah#1471) and refusing would make one schema applied across postgres, mysql and mariadb impossible.
